name: English Mild
title: English Mild: Style Guide | Craft Beer School
desc: English Mild explained: a low-strength, malty dark ale that packs flavour into 3 to 4 percent. How it tastes, Indian pairings and where to find it.
tagline: Big malt flavour at small strength. The beer you drink when you want to keep talking.
tastes:
Mild is one of England's oldest pub styles. In the past mild meant young, fresh beer as opposed to aged and soured stock, not low strength. Through the twentieth century it became the everyday ale of industrial towns, brewed weaker and darker, and today most milds sit between 3 and 4 percent.

The skill lies in getting real flavour into so little alcohol. Brewers use crystal, chocolate and sometimes brown malt to give caramel, toffee, cocoa, light coffee and dried fruit. They mash warm to leave some unfermentable sugar for body, so a good mild never tastes thin or watery. Hops are kept low and English, there for balance. English ale yeast adds a little fruit. Most milds are dark, but pale versions exist. The best ones are served fresh on cask with low carbonation, and they are made to be drunk by the pint over a long evening.

profile.look: Dark copper to dark brown, often near black, clear, with a modest tan head.
profile.aroma_flavour: Caramel, toffee, cocoa and light coffee from dark malts, some dried fruit, gentle earthy hops and soft yeast fruitiness.
profile.mouthfeel: Light to medium body that feels fuller than its strength, low to moderate carbonation, and a soft finish.
profile.ingredients: English mild or pale ale malt with crystal, chocolate or brown malt, a little English hop, and a fruity English ale yeast. Some use brewing sugars.

in_india: Mild is almost unknown in India, mostly because our market rewards strength, and a 3.5 percent dark beer is a hard sell on a menu. That is a shame. In the heat, a flavourful beer you can drink slowly without feeling it makes a lot of sense,. Cask conditioning is rare here, so any Indian version will be on keg. Ask brewers to make one.

pairings.why: The beer's malt sweetness softens the black pepper and kalpasi heat without adding alcohol burn.
Nutty peanuts and a soft, malty beer make a gentle, savoury match.
Rich minced meat and cocoa malt share a deep savouriness.
Ghee and gram flour sweetness meet the beer's toffee and caramel.

examples_note: We could not find a verified Indian mild yet. Ask your local brewpub, as it is an easy style for a brewer to make on request.
